claim.pdf_says: The whole of 2.4, including the general format "END PROGRAM program-name.", is inside the level-2 box drawn around the page content.
claim.why_it_matters: Every other element of 2.4 carries the ║ level-2 box marker; the general format line lost it, so it reads as level-1 content.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of page 237 (VI-5) shows one rectangle enclosing everything from '2.4 END PROGRAM HEADER' through the last line of GR2, and the line 'END PROGRAM program-name.' (END and PROGRAM underlined) sits inside it under 2.4.2. In page-237.md every heading and paragraph of 2.4 is wrapped in ║...║, but the <pre> general-format block has no ║. The transcription does mark level-2 content inside <pre> blocks elsewhere (for example the 66 RENAMES format at specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md:11553 carries ║ on each line), so this block breaks that convention and loses its level-2 box marking. Impact is limited: the 2.4 and 2.4.2 headings still carry ║, so a reader who goes by section containment still sees the format as level 2. A tool that reads level markers line by line, though, would classify the format as level 1.
verdict.corrected_description: On page 237 the PDF's level-2 box encloses the whole of 2.4, including the general format 'END PROGRAM program-name.'. The markdown <pre> block for that format has no ║ box marker, even though the transcription puts ║ on level-2 lines inside <pre> blocks elsewhere. The surrounding 2.4/2.4.2 headings keep ║, so containment still shows level 2, but a per-line level reader would see the format as level 1. Fix: wrap the format line in ║ ... ║.
